Why it matters

What is an ADU, and why now?

An Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) is a small, independent home on the same lot as your main house, with its own kitchen, bathroom and entrance. It works for aging parents, adult children, guests or long-term rental income.

Since February 2025, Massachusetts law allows one ADU by right in single-family zoning districts. A building permit and code compliance are still required, and towns can set local rules on things like setbacks and parking.

  • Up to 900 sq ft, or half the size of the main home, whichever is smaller
  • No special permit required in single-family zones
  • No owner-occupancy requirement under state law
  • Building permit and code compliance still required

Septic comes up early on the Cape

Many Cape Cod homes use septic systems, and adding a bedroom may require a septic review or upgrade. We talk this through at the first visit, so there are no surprises.

FAQ

ADUs questions, answered.

Do I need a special permit to build an ADU in Massachusetts?

In most single-family zoning districts, no. ADUs up to 900 sq ft are allowed by right. You'll still need a building permit, and your town may have local rules on things like setbacks and parking.

How big can my ADU be?

Up to 900 sq ft or half the size of your main home, whichever is smaller.

Can I rent out my ADU?

In general, yes. State law doesn't require the owner to live on the property. Some towns limit short-term rentals, so check your town's rules.

What about septic on Cape Cod?

Adding a bedroom may require a septic review or upgrade. We'll talk through this early, so there are no surprises.

How long does an ADU project take?

It depends on the type of ADU and the permit timeline in your town. You'll get a clear schedule with your estimate.
